display.title: The Baal Shem Tov and the Bear
display.summary_short: A Yiddish story told by a grandmother: young Yisroel, the future Baal Shem Tov, leads the cheder children singing to shul and fearlessly chases off a cruel man dressed as a bear.
display.summary_long: Told in Yiddish by a grandmother to her grandchildren. When the Baal Shem Tov was a small boy, his father told him: fear nothing except Hashem. As a young man he became a helper in the cheder. He brought the children to cheder, said Modeh Ani and washed negel vasser with them, and every Friday evening gathered them from house to house to go to shul for Lecha Dodi, singing Shabbos nigunim on the way while the angels in Heaven rejoiced. A cruel man who lived in the forest near the shul could not stand the singing. He put on a bear's skin and jumped out to frighten the children, until the mothers kept them home. Remembering his father's words, the young Baal Shem Tov took the children again, armed with a big stick, and beat the 'bear' until it ran off. On Sunday the man, aching all over, sent for him and admitted it had been him. The Baal Shem Tov davened for him, he recovered, and from then on he sat on his porch handing out kosher cookies and candy to the children on their way to shul.
display.lesson: Fear nothing but Hashem; Hashem loves to hear Jewish children singing on their way to shul and learning Torah.

advisories.note: A man disguised as a bear frightens children; the young Baal Shem Tov beats the 'bear' with a stick, and the man is hurt but recovers.
